h1: Agile IT Operations: Kanban, ITIL and DevOps in Practice
seo_title: Agile IT Operations: Kanban, ITIL and DevOps in Practice
meta_description: Agile IT operations explained: run incidents, requests and improvements with Kanban, reserved capacity, ITIL and DevOps, with a worked example and metrics.
excerpt: How IT operations teams apply Agile: one board for all work, an interrupt policy, capacity reserved from data, ITIL change enablement, DORA metrics and error budgets, with an illustrative worked example.
learning_objectives: Classify operations work into incidents, requests, improvement and maintenance and set a policy for each
Choose between Kanban, Scrum and Scrumban from the measured work mix
Size reserved capacity for unplanned work from eight or more weeks of data
Map ITIL 4 practices, including change enablement, to Agile ways of working
Calculate and interpret an error budget and a Little's Law cycle time estimate
Select flow, DORA and service metrics, using current DORA definitions

formulas.formula: Team capacity = people x focus hours per week
Mean unplanned effort = sum of weekly unplanned hours / weeks; share = mean / capacity
formulas.result: 708/8 = 88.5 h; 46.1%; range 36.5%-52.6%; 50% reservation (96 h) covers 6 of 8 weeks

formulas.formula: Little's Law: average cycle time = average WIP / average throughput
formulas.result: 1.6 weeks (8 working days); 0.8 weeks (4 working days)

formulas.formula: Monthly saving = volume x (hours before - hours after); payback = build effort / monthly saving
Change fail rate = failed changes / total changes
